actions.title: Understand
actions.description: Put numbers and ideas into words.
actions.prompt: A dashboard shows 120 orders in April, then 150 in May. How can I describe this change?
steps: Volume went from 120 to 150 orders: that is 30 additional orders.
Use April as the starting point: 30 ÷ 120 = 0.25, or 25%.
Ready to share: “In May, we received 30 more orders than in April, an increase of 25%.”
actions.summary: May had 150 orders, 30 more than April. The increase is 25%, using April as the baseline.

actions.title: Verify
actions.description: Check your reasoning before moving on.
actions.prompt: In a software specification, an €80 price receives a 15% discount. The expected result is €65. Is this reasoning consistent?
steps: The discount applies to €80. Fifteen per cent of €80 is €12.
The expected €65 result subtracts €15, rather than 15%. Check this assumption in your specifications. No code is changed.
actions.summary: A 15% discount on €80 gives €68. The expected €65 result confuses a 15% discount with subtracting €15. No code is changed.

actions.title: Convert
actions.description: Switch units without losing your train of thought.
actions.prompt: An order contains 24 bottles of 75 cL. What total volume in litres should I tell the customer?
steps: Ready to share: “Your order contains 18 litres in total, across 24 bottles.”
actions.summary: 24 bottles of 75 cL contain 18 litres in total. Each bottle contains 0.75 litres.

actions.title: Plan
actions.description: Turn available time into clear next steps.
actions.prompt: I have one hour to prepare a presentation, review my notes and leave some breathing room before a meeting.
steps: Preparation: spend 30 minutes on the main story and your materials.
Review: allow 20 minutes for your notes and transitions.
Buffer: leave 10 minutes to check your equipment and take a breath. The whole plan fits into one hour.
actions.summary: One hour: 30 minutes of preparation, 20 minutes of review and a 10-minute buffer. Adjust the balance to suit your priorities.

actions.title: Communicate
actions.description: Find the right words to explain a result.
actions.prompt: A customer wants to understand a 4% commission on a €2,500 sale. How can I explain it simply?
steps: The reference amount is the €2,500 sale.
The commission is €4 for every €100, making €100 in total.
Suggested wording: “For this €2,500 sale, the 4% commission comes to €100.”
actions.summary: “For this €2,500 sale, the 4% commission comes to €100. That is €4 for every €100.”

actions.title: Learn
actions.description: Make a concept yours, one step at a time.
actions.prompt: Course notes — chapter on percentages: a rate goes from 20% to 25%. Distinguish percentage points from relative change.
steps: Chapter takeaway: moving from 20% to 25% is an increase of 5 percentage points.
Relative change uses the initial rate: (25 − 20) ÷ 20 = 25%.
To revise: explain out loud why “5 points” and “a 25% increase” describe the same change using different reference points.
actions.summary: From 20% to 25%: +5 percentage points, or +25% relative to the initial rate. Points compare the rates directly; relative change uses the starting rate.
